plugins.name: Net Tools
plugins.author: Slashbar
plugins.description: Ports, sockets and the processes holding them

commands.name: Who Has This Port?
commands.body: p=$(tr -cd '0-9' | head -c 5); [ -n "$p" ] || { echo 'Type a port number first.'; exit 0; }; out=$(/usr/sbin/lsof -nP +c 0 -iTCP:$p -sTCP:LISTEN 2>/dev/null); [ -n "$out" ] && echo "$out" || echo "Nothing is listening on $p."
commands.description: Type a port number to see which process is listening on it.

commands.name: Common Dev Ports
commands.description: Just the ports dev servers usually grab — 3000, 5173, 8080 and friends.

commands.name: Listening Summary
commands.body: /usr/sbin/lsof -nP +c 0 -Fpcn -iTCP -sTCP:LISTEN 2>/dev/null | awk '/^c/{c=substr($0,2)} /^n/{n=substr($0,2); sub(/.*:/,"",n); print c, n}' | sort -u -k2,2n | awk '{printf "%-24s %s\n", $1, $2}'
commands.description: One tidy line per listening process and port.

commands.name: Established Connections
commands.description: What is actually talking to the network right now.

commands.name: Check Remote Port
commands.body: read -r line; h=$(echo "$line" | awk '{print $1}' | sed 's|.*://||;s|/.*||;s|:.*||'); p=$(echo "$line" | grep -oE '[0-9]+$'); p=${p:-443}; [ -n "$h" ] || { echo 'Type a host, optionally with a port: example.com 443'; exit 0; }; if nc -z -G 3 "$h" "$p" 2>/dev/null; then echo "open   $h:$p"; else echo "closed $h:$p"; fi
commands.description: Type "example.com 443" to see whether that port answers.

commands.name: My IP Addresses
commands.body: echo 'Local:'; ipconfig getifaddr en0 2>/dev/null; ipconfig getifaddr en1 2>/dev/null; echo 'Public:'; curl -s --max-time 4 https://api.ipify.org; echo
commands.description: Local interface addresses and the public one.
